text:
elaine: Heads-up — after the 09:00 rollout (merge PR#5123) we saw p99 token latency jump in euw2 A10 L4 cluster. Canary flagged it first :frowning:
samir: saw the alert, watching dashboards now. looks like KV cache evict rate up ~3x and batching latency up on long reqs
beth: can we confirm this is region-specific? I only see it in euw2-a10-l4, other clusters normal
elaine: yes only euw2-a10-l4. h100 and other pools unaffected. suspect kernel selector + new batching heuristic in the merge
nate: rolling logs — here are a couple snippets from the runtime on one affected pod:
```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kv_cache: evict_count=423 delta=3.2x
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] batcher: flush_ms_p50=11 -> 38 p99=120 -> 340
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] kernel_choice: selected=kselector_v2 alt=fallback_kernel
```
elaine: deploy-bot shows the canary (euw2-a10-l4/canary-3) rolled yesterday with PR#5123
deploy-bot: Canary deploy completed for merge PR#5123 at 2026-03-17T23:04:12Z
samir: I ran a short perf profile on the pod (perf-bot attached): top shows long sleeps in scheduler and a lot of iowait spikes. suspect NIC queue starvation causing pipeline stalls
perf-bot: Attached flamegraph url: https://perf.internal/fg/2041209876/1 (cc @samir)
beth: weird — batching change reduced eager flush threshold; on A10 with our NIC driver that increases small bursts and causes TX queue backlog under certain cross-tenant patterns
nate: eBPF trace from kernel shows repeated kthread wakeups at ~5ms intervals coinciding with kvcache evictions
```
k:task_wake: pid=3321 comm=batcher -> kselector_v2
net: tx_queue_full  iface=ens5 txq_len=512 drop=46
```
elaine: tried toggling kernel selector to fallback locally (kselector_v1) and latency dropped back to baseline in canary pod
samir: good test — can you push a non-prod patch to force kselector_v1 and run e2e perf?
elaine: pushed patch, canary run shows p99 back to normal, KV evict delta gone

elaine: conclusion so far: combination of kselector_v2 + new batching heuristic -> bursts that interact poorly with NIC driver on A10 L4 (cross-tenant noisy neighbor). Not purely CPU.
beth: options: revert PR#5123 (fast), force kselector_v1 on euw2-a10-l4 only (targeted), or tune batching thresholds and add NIC guardrail
samir: I'd prefer targeted mitigation: pin kernel selector to v1 for euw2-a10-l4 and roll batching tweak back from global to staged config, then iterate. Revert if needed
nate: I'm seeing noisy neighbor markers from host 10.23.142.9 — infra team will isolate and throttle that VM

infra-bot: Network throttle applied to host 10.23.142.9 (egress limit 200Mbps) — monitoring for 10m

elaine: after throttle p99 dipped ~30% but still slightly above baseline. suggests multi-factor: NIC + kv eviction behavior. we should bisect per-commit in PR#5123 to find exact change (kernel selection vs batching param)
samir: can we reproduce on a small A10 L4 perf cluster with synthetic noisy traffic? I'll spin one up and run the test harness (takes ~25m)
beth: note: PR#5123 included these changes: 1) kselector_v2 heuristic change 2) global batching flush_timeout drop 3) kvcache prefetch tweak — any or combo could be culprit
ate: (typo) nate -> nate
nate: started a bisect job: `./scripts/perf_bisect --range=main~10..main --target=euw2-a10-l4 --metric=p99`

deploy-bot: Bisect job 2041211002 started by nate for range main~10..main

samir: preliminary bisect narrows it to commit 3/10 in the series — the commit that adjusts batching flush_timeout (not the kernel selector commit)

elaine: interesting — so batching change exposes the kernel/NIC weakness, even if selector is less aggressive. Action plan:
- emergency: pin kselector_v1 for euw2-a10-l4 (rollout now)
- short-term: revert global batching flush change (revert PR#5123 batching part)
- mid-term: add NIC queue guardrail + backpressure in batcher on A10 pools

beth: I'll open a rollout-hold for global rollout until mitigations deployed (adding to release board)
samir: can we get a postmortem template pulled together after we stabilize? include perf traces, eBPF logs, and commit bisect notes

elaine: done — created issue INF-2045 with links to flamegraphs, bisect logs, and canary diffs

nate: rolled kselector pin to v1 in euw2-a10-l4; monitoring looks good so far :thumbsup:

elaine: thanks all — leaving rollout hold until batching revert lands and infra confirms noisy host stable. follow-ups: beth to own revert PR, samir to lead perf validation, nate to coordinate infra isolation. :white_check_mark:
